articles.title: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.mainIdea: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.summary: Argus Research: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term. The stock market got off to a volatile start in 2026, with a wide dispersion of returns among indices, sectors, industries, and individual stocks. The S&P 500 (SPX), Nasdaq, Nasdaq 100 (QQQ), and S&P 100 (OEX) oscillated between very small gains and losses, while the NYSE Composite rose 1.1%, the S&P MidCap 400 ripped higher by 1.3%, and the S&P SmallCap 600 popped 1%. Much of the buying after early-day weakness was seen in mid- and small-cap stocks. Information Technology stocks were all over the place, with SNDK ripping 16%, MU surging 11%, WDC popping 9%, LRCX soaring 8%, and TER and INTC gaining 7%. A number of these stocks were the largest gainers in 2025. On the flipside, APP plunged over 8%, PLTR declined 6%, and INTU and ADBE both lost 5%. That is an odd list of losers, as APP and PLTR saw huge 2025 gains and are considered market leaders, while INTU has been weak since July 2025 and ADBE has been a disaster since early 2024. The S&P 500 still appears to be tracing out a continuous inverse head-and-shoulders formation. To complete the pattern, the index must break above the recent closing highs near 6,930 for a few days and on higher volume. The Nasdaq and the QQQ appear to be forming symmetrical triangles, and we would like them to clear their prior highs of 23,959 and 635, respectfully, on increased volume (and for at least two days). The S&P MidCap 400 looks interesting as the index broke out to all-time highs on December 10 and 11 with well-above-average volume. The ETF then pulled back to its breakout area just above 600 twice before bouncing with a nice volume pickup on Friday. (Mark Arbeter, CMT) Related tickers mentioned: ADBE, EXPE, INCY, INTC, INTU, LRCX, MU, PLTR, ^GSPC, ^SP400, ^SP600.
